nrouter/auto.funded_by: credits or the plan's usage allowance
nrouter/auto.description: nRouter chooses the model for the task from the models available for automatic routing.

nrouter/promo.description: nRouter chooses the model from the promotional model set and charges the request to the organization's promotional credit, never to prepaid credits or a plan allowance. Promotional credit is spent only through this route: a request naming any other model, nrouter/auto included, never draws it. Spend is capped per organization by UTC windows set by nRouter (by default hourly none, daily $1, weekly $7, monthly $30; a week starts Monday 00:00 UTC). An empty balance is refused 402 insufficient_promo_credit and a used-up window 429 pot_spend_limit_exceeded, both before any provider egress. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses); response caching is off on this route, and web search, n > 1 and tool-billed features are refused 400 pot_route_feature_unsupported. x-nr-funding-source is promo.

nrouter/hack.description: nRouter chooses the model from the hackathon model set and charges the request to the organization's hackathon credit, never to prepaid credits or a plan allowance. Hackathon credit is spent only through this route. Same spend windows as nrouter/promo (by default hourly none, daily $1, weekly $7, monthly $30, UTC). An empty balance is refused 402 insufficient_hack_credit and a used-up window 429 pot_spend_limit_exceeded, both before any provider egress. Text wires only; response caching is off, and web search, n > 1 and tool-billed features are refused 400 pot_route_feature_unsupported. x-nr-funding-source is hack.

x-nr-latency-ms.description: Milliseconds from edge arrival until the response headers are ready. For a streamed response this is time-to-headers, not time to the final event, so it is not a total-generation figure. Stamped at the edge on every response the gateway produces, success or failure.

x-nr-trace-id.description: The OpenTelemetry trace ID for this request, absent when no valid trace exists. A client may also SEND x-nr-trace-id (and x-nr-session-id) to correlate its own spans; the value returned here is the gateway's, which always overwrites whatever arrived.

x-nr-request-cost.description: Exact cost in USD; absent when the model is unpriced

x-nr-total-tokens.description: Total token count, including cache tokens

x-nr-cache-read-tokens.description: Provider cache-read tokens; emitted only when nonzero

x-nr-cache-write-tokens.description: Provider cache-write tokens; emitted only when nonzero

x-nr-limit-source.description: Limit source on 429 and 402 responses; pot_window names a rolling spend-window limit on nrouter/promo or nrouter/hack

x-nr-budget-warning.description: A soft budget you configured was crossed by this request, which still served; absent otherwise. Value: <scope> soft_budget <spend>/<ceiling> — scope is org, team or user; spend is the USD already committed in the budget window before this request; ceiling is the hard budget; both to two decimals

x-nr-guardrails.description: Posture of the PRE-CALL guardrail chain for this request. ABSENT means this response makes no guardrail claim — /v1/models, the control plane, an auth refusal that never reached preflight — exactly as absence works for x-nr-limit-source. Absence is never "no guardrail applied"; that is the explicit token `none`. Published on every wire that runs a pre-call guardrail chain: the four text wires `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`, and the modality wires `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/audio/speech`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, `/v1/embeddings` and `POST /v1/videos`. It is ABSENT on the two FREE video collection routes, `GET /v1/videos/{id}` and `GET /v1/videos/{id}/content`, which resolve no chain at all — absence there is the contract, and `none` would wrongly assert that a chain was looked for.

value_semantics.none: No guardrail applied to this request. A legitimate state for a tenant who configured nothing, and the alarm for one who did.
value_semantics.monitor: A chain applied and nothing in it could have refused (warn/log trial modes only). It observed; it did not protect. Reporting this as `pass` would claim an enforcement that never existed.
value_semantics.redacted: An enforcing chain REWROTE part of the prompt before it reached the provider — PII or keyword redaction — and the request was then served (HTTP 200). The model did not see what you sent, so a response that quotes the prompt back quotes the rewritten one. Distinct from `pass` on purpose: `pass` means an enforcing chain found nothing to act on, and reporting a rewrite as `pass` hides the one case where request and prompt differ. WHAT was rewritten is deliberately withheld — see design_note.
value_semantics.pass: An enforcing chain inspected the whole request and allowed it.
value_semantics.partial: An enforcing chain ran but did not inspect the whole request. It means ONLY that some content went uninspected — never that something was acted on or rewritten, which is `redacted`. WHICH part went uninspected is deliberately withheld — see design_note. It is the ORDINARY answer on the two audio upload wires, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations`, not an anomaly there: a client that alarms on `partial` will alarm on every speech-to-text request it makes.
value_semantics.blocked: An enforcing chain refused the request. The one response that proves a control ran, so it is never silent about it.
value_semantics.unavailable: An enforcing chain could not run, so the request was refused WITHOUT being judged (HTTP 503, `error.type`/`error.code` "service_unavailable"). Distinct from `blocked` on purpose: the content was never assessed, so the correct client behaviour is to RETRY, not to rewrite the prompt. A 503 that reported `blocked` sent callers to change content that nothing had objected to. This header is what separates a guardrail-capacity 503 from any other one.

x-nr-guardrails.design_note: POSTURE ONLY, BY DESIGN (Rule #29; gateway rules 00-gateway-rules.md §4f gate 9). The token is the whole payload. Policy NAME, policy ID, detector family, RULE COUNT, and — for `partial` — WHICH channel went uninspected are all deliberately withheld, and widening this header to carry any of them is a security regression, not an improvement. A rule count moves when a policy moves, so a caller watching it maps a tenant's controls without ever tripping one; naming the uninspected channel hands an evader the smuggling route. That is why `partial` is a bare token and stays one. Match the value EXACTLY and case-sensitively (GuardrailStatus::from_wire is case-sensitive on purpose): an unrecognised token is unknown, never a guess at the nearest one.

x-nr-auth-reason.description: Machine-readable reason a virtual key was refused

x-nr-model-deprecated.description: Emitted when the served model is deprecated and will be retired

x-nr-deprecation-notice.description: Notice and successor guidance for a deprecated model

x-nr-response-cache.description: nRouter response-cache outcome for this request

x-nr-response-cache-age.description: Age in seconds of a response-cache hit

x-nr-compression.description: Prompt compression outcome for this request

x-nr-routing.description: Which chain entry answered: direct for the first entry, fallback:<n> for the entry n fallbacks deep. Absent on cache hits and refusals

x-nr-attempts.description: Provider calls made for this request, retries and failovers alike. Absent on cache hits and refusals

x-nr-intent.description: The top intent category evaluated by the preflight chain when intent classification runs on nrouter/auto

x-nr-funding-source.description: Which balance paid for this request: the plan's usage allowance, credits, promotional credit (promo-labeled models) or hackathon credit (hack-labeled models)

x-nr-allowance-reset.description: Seconds until the tightest usage-allowance window resets; sent on allowance-window 429s (equal to Retry-After) and the monthly 402 plan_allowance_exhausted

x-nr-tags.description: Custom spend tags for this request, formatted as key=value,key2=value2. Relayed to spend records in nrouter.spend_logs.

x-nr-compress.description: Prompt compression request toggle. Set 'on', 'true', '1' to enable prompt compression; 'off', 'false', '0' to disable.

x-nr-trace-id.description: Client OpenTelemetry trace ID for correlating spans across client and gateway.

x-nr-session-id.description: Client session identifier for correlating multi-turn conversation steps.

x-nr-client-language.description: Client SDK implementation language, automatically set by each official SDK.

error.code: string (OPTIONAL — absent on most refusals; model it as nullable/optional or a strict decoder will fail on a 401, 404 or 429)

error_envelope.description: A refusal body always carries `error.type` and `error.message`, and carries `error.code` only where the gateway can name one of the keys under `errors` — that table is the whole set, and it spans refusals at every status, for example a guardrail refusal at either end, a guardrail-capacity 503, the 402 budget refusals, and request-shape 400s such as `input_too_large`, `fallback_not_allowed`, `guardrail_not_found` and `invalid_request`. It is ABSENT elsewhere rather than invented, because a code outside this spec is a code no client's table contains. Classify on `code` when present, then on `type`, then on the HTTP status. Never classify on `message`: it is prose written for a person and it changes.

type_values.gateway_error: The gateway's own error type for a refusal that carries no more specific type — authentication, credits, model, rate limit. The HTTP status is the discriminator.
type_values.guardrail_blocked: A guardrail refused this request: the PROMPT was refused pre-call (HTTP 400), or an OUTPUT guardrail withheld an otherwise successful provider response (HTTP 400, or a terminal SSE error frame inside a 200 on a stream). One `type` for both ends, so a client branches once.
type_values.service_unavailable: A dependency the gateway needs was unavailable (HTTP 503), including an enforcing guardrail that could not run — `x-nr-guardrails: unavailable` distinguishes that case. NOT a content refusal: retry rather than rewriting the prompt.

error_envelope.join_key_note: Always present on every response, success or refusal. It is the only join key between a refusal shown to a user and the request record behind it, so surface it wherever an error is displayed.

guardrail_blocked.description: A guardrail denied the request (pre-call) or withheld the response (post-call)

detection.buffered: HTTP 400 AND (`error.code` == "guardrail_blocked" OR `error.type` == "guardrail_blocked" OR the message contains "guardrail"). The first two arms are the contract: both ends of the request now send that one token, as `code` and as `type`. The message arm is a COMPATIBILITY fallback and is required for any gateway older than this spec version, where a pre-call block arrived as `type` "gateway_error" with a message beginning "request blocked by a guardrail" and no `code` at all. Use it only after the first two have missed — never as a general classification rule.
detection.streaming: A stream's status line is already sent when an output guardrail decides, so the cut arrives INSIDE a 200 response as a terminal `event: error` SSE frame whose data is the same {"error":{"type":"guardrail_blocked",...}} document. A streaming client that only inspects the HTTP status will read a withheld response as a successful, empty one.
detection.not_2xx_buffered: On a buffered route a post-call block over a successful upstream response is converted to 400 before the response is built, so it never arrives as a 2xx. A 2xx that nonetheless carries an error envelope is a provider-origin document passed through unchanged, not a guardrail verdict.

model_not_found.description: Model unknown or not visible to this key; a former model alias name is now an unknown model

rate_limit_exceeded.description: A rate limit was exceeded (RPM, TPM, RPS or RPD), or an 8-hour/daily/weekly nrouter/auto allowance window is used up (x-nr-limit-source: plan_window_h8|plan_window_day|plan_window_week; Retry-After and x-nr-allowance-reset carry the wait in seconds). With extra usage turned on in Billing, allowance overflow is funded from credits instead of refused; see x-nr-limit-source. A used-up promo or hack spend window answers pot_spend_limit_exceeded instead

service_unavailable.description: A required gateway dependency is unavailable. Also covers an enforcing GUARDRAIL that could not run, in which case `x-nr-guardrails: unavailable` is present: the request was refused WITHOUT being judged, so retry it rather than rewriting the prompt. Both are transient and nothing was charged.

plan_allowance_exhausted.description: The plan's monthly usage allowance is used up (HTTP 402; the 8-hour, daily and weekly windows answer 429 rate_limit_exceeded instead). It resets at the next billing period (see x-nr-allowance-reset); no Retry-After is sent. With extra usage turned on in Billing, allowance overflow is funded from credits instead of refused.

plan_required.description: An organization's legacy subscription plan usage allowance is paused pending payment. Pay-as-you-go organizations are served nrouter/auto and named models from credits and do not receive this code. Promo- and hack-labeled models are funded from their promotional or hackathon credit first (falling back to credits when available) and never receive this code.

input_too_large.description: The request's input exceeds the served model's context window. Refused before any provider egress, so nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Permanent for this body: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window.

max_output_tokens_too_large.description: The requested output ceiling (max_tokens / max_output_tokens) exceeds what the served model allows. Refused before any provider egress, so nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Lower the ceiling; it is not clamped for you, because silently changing it changes what the request costs.

model_denied_by_org.description: The requested model, or a model named in nrouter_fallbacks, is on the organization's model deny list. A deny always wins over an allow list, and a denied model is also removed from nrouter/auto and promo/hack pot eligibility. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

model_denied_by_team.description: The requested model, or a model named in nrouter_fallbacks, is on the deny list of the team this virtual key belongs to. A deny always wins over an allow list, and a denied model is also removed from nrouter/auto and promo/hack pot eligibility. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

model_denied_by_key.description: The requested model, or a model named in nrouter_fallbacks, is on this virtual key's own model deny list. A deny always wins over an allow list, and a denied model is also removed from nrouter/auto and promo/hack pot eligibility. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

fallback_not_allowed.description: A model named in the request's nrouter_fallbacks list cannot be used as a fallback target by this virtual key: the key cannot route it, or it is nrouter/auto, an allowance model or another model that is not offered as a fallback target. On a request for nrouter/auto it is also returned for a target whose own hold for this request is above the largest hold a single request may take. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

insufficient_promo_credit.description: A request for a promo-labeled model was refused because neither the organization's available promotional credit nor its prepaid credit balance can cover the request's hold. Promotional credit has no cash value and is spent only on promo-labeled models. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

insufficient_hack_credit.description: A request for a hack-labeled model was refused because neither the organization's available hackathon credit nor its prepaid credit balance can cover the request's hold. Hackathon credit has no cash value and is spent only on hack-labeled models. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

pot_spend_limit_exceeded.description: A promo- or hack-funded request would take the organization's spend on that pot past one of its windows (set by nRouter; by default hourly none, daily $1, weekly $7, monthly $30; x-nr-limit-source: pot_window) and no prepaid credit balance was available to overflow into. Windows are UTC calendar buckets: the hour, the day, the ISO week starting Monday 00:00 UTC, and the month. The message names the window that refused and when it resets. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

pot_route_feature_unsupported.description: A promo- or hack-funded request asked for a feature those pots do not fund when no prepaid credit balance is available: web search (nrouter_web_search), more than one choice (n > 1), or a tool-billed feature. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Remove the feature or add prepaid credits.

guardrail_not_found.description: A guardrail id or name in the request's nrouter_guardrails list is not owned by this organization. Refused rather than ignored: a silently dropped guardrail is a request the caller believes was inspected and was not. Nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

image_input_unsupported.description: The request to nrouter/auto includes an image, and no model available for automatic routing on this endpoint accepts image input. Refused before any provider egress, so nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Permanent for this body: remove the image or name a model that accepts images.

supported_endpoints.note: Collection is free — the customer is billed when the video is CREATED, not when its status is polled or its bytes are downloaded.
Collection is free — the customer is billed when the video is CREATED, not when its status is polled or its bytes are downloaded.

nrouter_prompt_variables.description: Jinja2 variables for the prompt template

nrouter_cache.description: Use nRouter's tenant-isolated response cache for buffered text requests. Set false to force provider egress; streams are never cached.

nrouter_fallbacks.description: Per-request fallback chain: up to 4 model names, tried in order when the primary cannot be served. `model` stays the primary and is never listed here. This REPLACES the organization's fallback policy for this one call and is not merged with it. A target this virtual key cannot route — and nrouter/auto, nrouter/promo, nrouter/hack, an allowance model or any other model that is not offered as a fallback target — is refused with 400 fallback_not_allowed before any provider egress. On a request for nrouter/auto the list replaces the fallbacks nrouter/auto would choose: the model it chooses is tried first, then these targets in order, and an empty list means no fallback. One hold covers the whole chain, sized to its dearest entry; when the funds cannot cover it the request is refused 402 before any provider call, and a target is never dropped to make it fit. A fallback is tried only when the provider cannot take the request, and the request is charged once, for the model that answered. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses).

nrouter_optimize.description: Selection strategy for a request on nrouter/auto only. "quality" (the organization default) serves the best model for the task, chosen by the decision model; "cost" serves, among the models fit for the task, the one with the lowest list rate. It overrides the organization's saved Router Settings strategy for this one request. Any other value, a non-string, or sending the field with any model other than nrouter/auto is refused with 400 invalid_request naming the field. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses).

nrouter_guardrails.description: Per-request guardrail selection: up to 8 guardrail ids or names owned by this organization. ADD-ONLY — the listed guardrails run IN ADDITION to the ones already assigned to the key, team or organization, and a request can never remove, relax or replace an assigned guardrail or the platform moderation floor. An id or name the organization does not own is refused with 400 guardrail_not_found rather than ignored, because a silently dropped guardrail is a request the caller believes was inspected and was not. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses).

spend_row_metadata_fields.$comment: RESPONSE surface, not a request body. These are the customer-visible keys the dashboard spend-row route (GET /api/nrouter-proxy/spend/by-key) returns inside a log row's `metadata`. Sending one as a request field is a defect: the gateway does not read them and forwards them to the provider verbatim. Derived from nrouter-app src/lib/logs/sanitize-log-metadata.ts (CUSTOMER_FACING_NROUTER_META_KEYS, the allowlist the drawer scrubs against) — re-derive, never retype. Every nrouter_* key not listed here is gateway-internal and is stripped before a customer ever sees it. The examples gate enforces the nrouter_ namespace only; `tags` is the caller's own key, published here to document the surface, with nothing to refuse.

nrouter_cost.description: What the customer is CHARGED for the request, in USD; null when unpriced, never a zero.

nrouter_tenancy.description: The caller's own organization/team/user identity, resolved at authentication.

nrouter_modality.description: Which modality the request was billed as (text, image, audio, video, embedding).

nrouter_units.description: The unit the charge was measured in (tokens, images, characters, seconds).

nrouter_stream.description: Whether the request was served as a stream.

nrouter_withheld_by_guardrail.description: The response was blocked by a guardrail and never delivered to the caller.

nrouter_model.description: The model actually served: the model named in the request, a fallback you configured, or the model nrouter/auto, nrouter/promo or nrouter/hack chose.

nrouter_routing.description: How the request was routed, as { attempts, served_rank, fallback_used, source }. `attempts` is the number of provider calls this request made (1 when the primary answered first). `served_rank` is the 0-based position in the chain that answered, so 0 is the primary. `fallback_used` is true when the model served was not the primary. `source` names which chain was in force: the organization's fallback policy, or a per-request nrouter_fallbacks list. Pairs with nrouter_model, which names the model that answered.

nrouter_request_id.description: The id the customer quotes in support; pairs with the x-nr-request-id response header.

nrouter_response_cache.description: hit or miss for an eligible buffered text request; null when caching does not apply.

nrouter_postflight.description: Bounded after-provider outcome projection, itself behind a field-level allowlist.

nrouter_guardrails.description: Response side, as { redacted: bool }: true when a guardrail rewrote the caller's own prompt before it was sent on. This is not the request field of the same name (extra_body_fields.nrouter_guardrails), which selects guardrails for one call.

nrouter_timings.description: How long each phase of the request took, in milliseconds, keyed by phase name (for example key_auth, rate_limit, guardrails_scoring, reserve, provider, post_call). Phases run in order and do not overlap, except intent_classify and content_scoring, which are time already inside guardrails_scoring. `edge_to_row` is the measured time from the request arriving to its log row being written, and is never a sum of the others. A phase that was not recorded has no key. `provider` is the whole provider call, not time to first token: for a stream, time to first token is the row's completionStartTime minus its startTime.

nrouter_auto_routing.description: Present on a request for nrouter/auto: how the model was chosen, as { mode, source, task, task_outcome, model_outcome }. `mode` is off, shadow or enforce. `source` is signals (chosen from the request's own shape: reasoning asked for, input length, tools) or decision (chosen by nRouter's model-selection step). `task` is the task type, present only when `task_outcome` is answered. `task_outcome` and `model_outcome` are one of answered, low_confidence, invalid, timeout, error, skipped, cancelled, not_asked or not_enabled. The served model is nrouter_model.

nrouter_checks.description: What each preflight check decided, as { version, model_access, rate_limit, rate_limit_dimension, concurrency }. Each check is allowed or refused. `rate_limit_dimension` (rpm, tpm, tps or rpd) appears only beside a refused rate_limit, when the limit that refused is known. A check that did not run has no key, so an absent key never means allowed.

nrouter_trace.description: Per-step request trace, as { v, steps, coverage }. `steps` is a list of START events { i, p?, k: "s", n, t } and END events { i, k: "e", t, o }: `i` pairs a START with its END, `p` is the enclosing step's `i`, `n` is the step name, `t` is the offset in microseconds from the request arriving, and `o` is the outcome (ok, refused, error, timeout, cancelled, panicked). `coverage` says what the trace does and does not include: `ends_at` is row_snapshot (the trace stops when the log row is written, so work after that is absent), `truncated` and `undeclared` count events that were dropped, and `unfinished` lists the `i` of steps still open at that point. Time between one step's END and the next step's START is untraced. Rows written before per-step tracing shipped carry no such key.

nrouter_web_search_requests.description: How many web searches the request ran: a count, never an amount. Present only when at least one search ran; the search charge is already inside nrouter_cost.

nrouter_usage.description: The token breakdown the charge was computed from: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens_1h, cache_read_input_tokens, audio_input_tokens, audio_output_tokens, web_search_requests and code_interpreter_containers. Counts only, no prices.

tags.description: The caller's own request tags, echoed back; additive and never authoritative for tenancy.
